questions.q: What is the safer framing for AI in a data engineering job, per this lesson?
options: AI should never be used by data engineers under any circumstances
AI as a productivity multiplier on skills you already have, not a replacement for having them
AI as a full replacement for understanding the pipeline
AI replaces the need to learn PySpark or KQL
questions.explain: A data engineer who already knows what good output looks like can use AI to go faster and catch mistakes. Someone who doesn't has no way to catch a bad answer.

questions.q: Why does the 'replacement' framing for AI go wrong, according to this lesson?
options: Because AI models are always factually correct
Because AI cannot generate any code at all
Because the person using it has no way to catch a wrong answer if they never understood the underlying skill
Because replacement framing is technically identical to multiplier framing
questions.explain: Ships whatever the model hands back, unchecked — the same gap Lesson 58's 'Evaluating AI Output for Correctness' makes explicit.

questions.q: Which of these is something AI is genuinely good at in a data engineering context, per this lesson?
options: Drafting boilerplate code and explaining unfamiliar code or stack traces
Guaranteeing generated logic is correct
Seeing your real Eventstream payload without you showing it
Knowing your specific business rules without being told
questions.explain: Boilerplate, explaining unfamiliar code, first drafts, and summarizing long logs or schemas are the concrete strengths this lesson names.

questions.q: Why can't an AI model know that `order_status = 'CANCELLED'` should be excluded from a revenue calculation on its own?
options: Because CANCELLED orders don't exist in real systems
Because business rules like that are specific to your data and have to be told to the model explicitly, every time
Because AI models can read database constraints directly
Because revenue calculations are illegal to automate
questions.explain: Knowing your data's business rules is called out as something AI is not good at unless you supply that context yourself.

questions.q: What does this bonus chapter explicitly NOT claim to do?
options: Mention data quality or documentation
Cover Copilot inside Microsoft Fabric at all
Discuss retrieval-augmented generation
Replace the system design, DP-700, Fabric, Databricks, or DE Foundations material that came before it
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit: AI tools sit on top of the foundational skills from earlier courses and lessons — they don't substitute for them.
